speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development whether there are efforts to work with other Ministries on youth mental health awareness amongst parents and on equipping parents with mental health awareness and response skills to better support children and youths in the environment of their own homes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Through these programmes, parents learn to better communicate with their children and to manage their children’s emotions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: MOE also provides practical tips and resources to parents through platforms such as Parent Kit, Schoolbag articles, "Ask Me Anything About …" Facebook Live sessions and through their "Parenting with You" Instagram account.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: These resources support parents in identifying signs and sources of stress in their children, building resilience in their children and taking care of their children’s mental well-being.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For students-at-risk, schools and Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) provide parents with timely updates on their children’s state of mental health and work with them to ensure care and support is provided where needed.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic posed new challenges and highlighted the importance of strengthening the mental health and well-being of our youth.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: To help parents better support their children, Families for Life (FFL) launched the #FFLShareTheCare online video series during the circuit breaker period.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: MSF also offers evidence-based parenting programmes such as the Positive Parenting Programme, or Triple P, that equips parents with simple and practical strategies to build strong, healthy relationships with their child, up to age 16, and confidently manage their child’s behaviour.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Currently, Triple P is available via an e-learning platform, Triple P Online (TPOL) or via video-conferencing platforms such as Zoom.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Other digital resources have also been developed to equip parents with the information and tools to support their children’s mental well-being.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Temasek Foundation, with support from the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC), has developed a "My Mental Health" microsite to address mental health challenges arising from the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Another website, Mindline.sg, is a joint initiative by Ministry of Health Office for Healthcare Transformation (MOHT), MSF, National Council of Social Service and IMH.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: A one-stop repository for resources and tools, Mindline.sg provides support and self-care tools specifically for care-givers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: While these programmes and resources help provide families with education and awareness on youth mental health and mental well-being, some of them may require further support and assistance.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Families facing marital and family issues, and/or parenting stress can approach any of our Family Service Centres or FSCs, or the online counselling service set up in April 2020 by MSF with the Community Psychology Hub.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Apart from these Government-led initiatives, over 1,500 youths, parents, care-givers and individuals from the social sector and mental health professionals came together to form the Youth Mental Well-being Network, to which MOE, MSF and MOH lend support.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Members include both individuals and organisations such as Campus PSY, which stands for "Peer Support for Youths", which promotes mental health awareness and peer support amongst youth, and Acceset, which aims to improve the mental well-being of youths through technology and research.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Members have been discussing various initiatives and ideas to enhance youth mental well-being, some of which are on equipping parents to better support their children’s mental health.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Network continues to welcome contributions from anyone who would like to join and make an impact in this space.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We will continue to work with anyone and any agency or individuals, who will come together with us, to help parents better support their children’s mental health and well-being.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Are there challenges to its roll-out, if any, and whether the Triple P Programme is on track to meet its scaled up targets, if it does have a plan for scaling up?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Triple P has, in fact, proven to be quite effective.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We have parents coming back to tell us that they now have greater parenting competence.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, we are happy to share some of these encouraging results.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, with this result, we hope that more parents could come onboard, join us for these online programmes, invest some of the time and energy, so that they can learn better parenting tips and be onboard with us on the programme.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: To add on to my supplementary question, I noted that the current Triple P efforts are quite focused on delivery via digital platforms.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Are there any plans by MOE to work with community partners or, perhaps, even PA, to bring some of this awareness or publicity about these programmes into the community, so that parents who may not naturally gravitate towards finding information online also will be accessed, in terms of having this information about the programme reach them.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We are now leveraging quite a bit on the online platforms because of the current situation that we are in, because of the pandemic situation that we are in.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Hopefully, the participation rate can be further boosted over time.
